1. This appeal is preferred by the claimants against the common judgment and award passed by the learned Land Reference Court, Beed in Land Acquisition Reference No.752 of 1987 dated 23.12.1999, by which, the claimants' claim for enhanced amount of compensation was dismissed.

1 2.

Learned Advocate Mr. R. D. Kawade, appearing for the appellants pointed out that the house nos.13/1+2 and 14/1+2 situated at village Laul, Tq. Majalgaon, Dist. Beed were acquired for 'Majalgaon Reservoir under the Jayakwadi Project' as per the notification dated 24.03.1983, issued under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

3. Learned Advocate for the appellants pointed out the pleadings and the evidence and submitted that the documentary evidence was not properly appreciated, the e-statement of the award of the Land Acquisition Officer at Exhibit 18 was relied upon without proving its contents.
The conclusions in paragraph nos.16 and 25 of the impugned judgment are not legal and correct.

It fails to appreciate the evidence of Ramhari, PW-3, who conducted the valuation of the acquired houses of the claimants and submitted the report as per the Exhibit 91, which, however, was not believed.

4. Learned AGP Mr. S. G. Joshi, appearing for the respondent- State submitted that, like these appellants, some other appellants' whose claims were dismissed, have preferred the appeals before this Court, which were also dismissed by this Court.

In the reasons of the impugned judgment in paragraph no.25, the learned Reference Court concluded that the valuation of the Land Acquisition Officer was wrong as it was more than the market value, which was already fa-1217-2003 awarded to the other claimants.
He further argued that the reasons as to the sale instance and the earlier judgment of the learned Reference Court are legal and correct and no interference is warranted in it.

It is lastly prayed to dismiss the appeal.
5.
Perused the Record and Proceedings, particularly the impugned judgment and the evidence on record.

The appellants have adduced oral evidence and also relied upon the report of the valuer at Exhibit-91, the sale instance at Exhibit-40 and also the judgment of the learned Reference Court in earlier Land Acquisition Reference No.481 of 1986 at Exhibit 19.

This Court perused the oral evidence of the Valuer and the impugned judgments, in paragraph nos.21, 24 and 25, the learned Reference Court has held that, to the extent of 60%, the report is acceptable and to the extent of 40%, report is held unacceptable.
The learned Reference Court in Paragraph no.25, has rightly held that the compensation awarded by the Special Land Acquisition Officer could be fixed by the Court on the basis of the said report.
It held that more than sufficient amount of compensation is awarded by the Land Acquisition Officer.

6. On re-appreciation of the entire evidence and grounds of objections of this appeal, this Court is of the view that the evidence is properly appreciated and the expert's evidence is rightly partly relied upon.
Further, this Court while deciding the appeals of other fa-1217-2003 claimants, whose claims were rejected, dismissed the appeal.
If all these aspects are considered together, this Court is of the view that there is no substance in the grounds of objections of the appeal.
The reasons and findings of the learned Reference Court are legal and correct and there is no scope for interference in it.
The decision of the learned Reference Court is correct.
The proper compensation is awarded by the Land Acquisition Officer to the claimants.
Therefore, the First Appeal deserves to be dismissed as it sans merit.

Hence, the following order:
ORDER a. First Appeal is dismissed with no orders as to costs.
b. Pending Civil Applications, if any, stand disposed of.
